name: Iaculo
body:
Iaculo
CR 1

You just hear a faint hiss before a tiny, multicolored serpent plunges toward you from a branch above, its body rigid as an arrow, aiming for your throat.

XP 400
N Tiny animal
Init +2; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 14, flat-footed 12 (+2 Dex, +2 size)
hp 11 (2d8+2)
Fort +4, Ref +5, Will +1

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., climb 30 ft.
Melee bite +5 (1d2-2)
Special Attacks impaling dive +5 (1d6 plus impale)

STATISTICS

Str 4, Dex 15, Con 13, Int 2, Wis 12, Cha 4
Base Atk +1; CMB +3 (+7 with grapple); CMD 10 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Weapon Finesse
Skills Climb +20, Perception +5, Stealth +14; Racial Modifiers +4 Climb, +4 Stealth

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Familiar

The master of a iaculo familiar gains a +3 bonus on Climb checks.

Impaling Dive (Ex)

A iaculo can drop on a victim from a high place, stiffening its body like an arrow in a gore attack. If the attack hits, it deals 1d6 points of piercing damage and the iaculo stabs through its prey, leaving part of its body inside it and effectively impaling it. This functions as the attach universal monster ability. At the beginning of its turn, an impaling iaculo automatically deals another 1d6 points of damage and can also try to bite its victim. A target who manages to remove the iaculo from its body suffers the same damage as having it attached in a round.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forests
Organization solitary or hail (1-20)
Treasure none

Iaculi (“javelin snakes”) are snakes able to briefly stiffen their bodies to the hardness of wood or metal. They are great climbers and live mostly on trees, waiting for passing prey to dive upon and transfix. Jaculi are not venomous; if one of them fails to impale a victim, it will most likely flee and maybe try to climb another tree to attempt a new dive. This is why iaculi are more dangerous when attacking in a group.

An average adult iaculo is 3 ft. long and weighs 2 lbs.

Iaculo are snakes that have developed a unique method of hunting prey. They climb trees and await prey passing below.

These reddish-brown serpents coil and then straighten in a sudden motion, flinging itself from a tree while ribbed wings spring out from its sides, guiding it with deadly trajectory as it plummets like a spear toward its target. The iaculo’s head is angular and ends in a sharp point above its mouth, which is actually a fang that grows up through the front of its head. This point is hard and sharp enough to penetrate flesh and even armor with the iaculo’s mass and speed behind it.

The iaculo folds in its wings in the moment before it strikes, looking much like a spear or ballista bolt as it plunges into its target.
